oneLiner: 按端到端的“流程”而非部门职能来设计工作；再造则是推倒重来而非修修补补。
oneLinerEn: Design work around end-to-end processes rather than functions; reengineering means tearing it up, not tidying it.
detail: 面对流程，管理界有两套打法。一套是迈克尔·哈默与詹姆斯·钱皮 1993 年在《企业再造》里鼓吹的彻底重设计：对流程做根本再思考、推倒重来，以求在成本、质量、速度上取得飞跃——它启发了无数公司，但高失败率也让“再造”一度名声复杂。更稳健的日常做法是流程管理：把价值流显式描绘出来、度量周期时间与缺陷率、持续小幅改进。两者共同的盲点常是“人”——流程改了、考核与权责没跟着改就会反弹；再造若只当裁员工具、而非真正重构做事方式，也很容易昙花一现。因此成功的关键不在有没有画出一张新流程图，而在绩效、激励与权责、信息是否随之同步改弦——否则再漂亮的蓝图也会悄悄退回旧轨道。
detailEn: Toward process, management offers two playbooks. One is the radical redesign Michael Hammer and James Champy championed in Reengineering the Corporation (1993): rethink a process from the ground up and rebuild it anew to leap in cost, quality and speed—it inspired countless firms, yet a high failure rate left "reengineering" with a checkered reputation. The steadier day-to-day path is process management: map the value flow explicitly, measure cycle time and defect rate, and improve in small continuous steps. The shared blind spot of both is people—change the process while pay, appraisal and authority stay put and it rebounds; treat reengineering as a headcount axe rather than a genuine reweaving of how work gets done, and the gains prove fleeting.

oneLiner: 计划—执行—检查—处置，把改进变成不断转圈的小步实验。
oneLinerEn: Plan-Do-Check-Act: turn improvement into small experiments that keep cycling.
detail: 休哈特在 1939 年提出循环雏形（PDSA，把 Check 改为 Study：不只对数据，要解释为何），戴明 1950 年起在日本把它讲成管理方法，遂称戴明环。四拍的纪律在于不得跳拍：先以假说形式写清成因与对策（而不是直接上措施），小范围试行并预先定义看什么数据，检查时区分预期与实际而非只报成功，有效才把做法标准化、无效则回到计划再转一圈。它的精神是“用数据代替拍脑袋、用小步迭代代替大规划”，是精益、六西格玛与持续改进的共同节律。两个常见走形：只转 Plan-Do 而不真做 Study 那一拍（把试行的异常当成噪声抹掉），以及把它当个人生产力工具用——戴明晚年反复强调，循环的对象是流程而非人的自律，没有管理层把“标准化后的改进必须被采纳”接住，它就只能在小圈子里空转。
detailEn: Shewhart sketched the cycle in 1939 as PDSA — Study rather than Check, since one explains data instead of merely comparing it; Deming taught it in Japan from 1950 as a management method, hence the ring with his name. The discipline is in not skipping beats: state cause and countermeasure as a hypothesis rather than jumping to action, run it small with the data to be watched defined in advance, study the gap between prediction and result instead of reporting success, and standardise only if it worked — otherwise return to Plan. Its spirit is data over decree and iteration over grand planning, which makes it the shared rhythm underneath lean, Six Sigma and continuous improvement. Two common corruptions: spinning Plan-Do without a serious Study, where the trial's anomalies are smoothed away as noise, and using it as personal productivity — Deming spent his last years insisting the object of the cycle is the process, not the worker's self-discipline; unless management receives the rule that a standardised improvement must be adopted, the wheel spins in a small circle.

oneLiner: 质量是全员、全过程的责任：以客户为中心、持续改进、用统计说话。
oneLinerEn: Quality is everyone's job across the whole process: customer-focused, continually improved, argued with statistics.
detail: 全面质量管理把质量从一线检验员的事提升为整个组织的哲学。费根堡姆 1951 年提出这一术语，朱兰与戴明则把它塑造成战后日本制造的根基：预防优于检验、管理层担的责大于一线、约 85% 的质量问题源于系统而非工人。它催生了一系列落地工具——统计过程控制、质量功能展开、品管圈，也把戴明奖（1951）、波多里奇国家质量奖（1987）与 ISO 9000 族标准推向了世界。它的失败常因被当成运动式口号：缺少长期投入与真正的授权时，“全员质量”就退化成“全员填表”。六西格玛可视为它的度量强化版。它的精髓是把质量变成人人可谈、可测、可改进的日常语言，而非某个部门的专属指标。
detailEn: Total quality management raised quality from an inspector's job to the philosophy of the whole organization. Feigenbaum coined the term in 1951, and Juran and Deming shaped it into the bedrock of postwar Japanese manufacturing: prevention beats inspection, management owns far more responsibility than the front line, and some 85 percent of quality problems stem from the system, not the worker. It spawned a toolkit—statistical process control, quality function deployment, quality circles—and propelled the Deming Prize (1951), the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award (1987) and the ISO 9000 family worldwide. It fails when treated as a campaign slogan: without long investment and real empowerment, "everyone does quality" decays into "everyone fills forms." Six Sigma is best read as its metrology-hardened successor.

oneLiner: 用 DMAIC 把缺陷压到百万分之三点四级别——靠数据与流程变异，而非灵光一现。
oneLinerEn: Use DMAIC to drive defects toward 3.4 per million — through data and variation, not flashes of insight.
detail: 六西格玛在摩托罗拉成形（1986 年前后）、在通用电气发扬（韦尔奇把它当作人才工程），名字来自统计：一西格玛是一个标准差，距“零缺陷”六个标准差意味着百万分之三点四的缺陷率。主干流程是 DMAIC：界定问题、测量现状、分析根因、改进流程、控制成果，每一环都要求统计证据而不是轶事，并以绿带/黑带的腰带体系培养骨干。它的真实杀伤力在两个地方：一是把“问题”定义到可测量（CTQ 树把客户语言拆成指标），二是控制阶段把改进锁进标准作业而不至三周后反弹。适用边界同样明确：它擅长有稳定数据、重复发生的流程变异消差；对高度模糊、以创意为主或根因实为激励而非波动的工作就水土不服，而且黑带项目制天然容易堆砌“为了项目而项目”的垃圾——这是它 2000 年代后退潮的主因之一。
detailEn: Six Sigma was formed at Motorola (around 1986) and amplified at General Electric, where Welch ran it as a talent programme; the name is statistical — one sigma is one standard deviation, and sitting six away from zero defects implies roughly three-and-a-half parts per million. The spine is DMAIC: define the problem, measure the current state, analyse root cause, improve the process, control the gain, with each stage demanding statistical evidence rather than anecdote, and a belt system (green, black) manufacturing the people who can run it. Its real force lives in two places: forcing a problem into something measurable (critical-to-tree translation from customer language into metrics), and the control phase locking the fix into standard work so it does not rebound in three weeks. The boundary is equally clear: it excels at reducing variation in stable, data-rich, repetitive processes, and turns clumsy on ambiguous, creative work or where the true cause is an incentive rather than a process — and its project-portfolio logic invites work created to justify projects, one reason the fashion receded after 2000.

oneLiner: 大野耐一列出七类不创造客户价值的浪费，逐一识别并消除。
oneLinerEn: Ohno named seven wastes that add no customer value; spot and remove each.
detail: 精益生产脱胎于丰田生产方式，其两大支柱是“准时化”（只在需要的时候、按需要的量生产，压低库存与等待）与“自动化”（特指带人机分离之意的那种——机器一旦异常就自动停机，人绝不做机器人的看守）。大野耐一归纳出七种浪费：过度生产（常被视为万恶之源，因为它掩盖其余所有问题）、等待、搬运、过度加工、库存、多余动作与缺陷返工，并主张到现场把价值流中不创造价值的环节逐一揪出。精益把“消除浪费、持续改善”变成每个人每天的纪律，靠看板拉动生产、靠员工发现问题即拉绳停线。这套框架后来溢出车间，走进软件、医疗与服务业，也成为“精益创业”那套“最小可行产品、快速验证”的母体。
detailEn: Lean production grew out of the Toyota Production System, whose two pillars are just-in-time — make only what is needed, when needed, in the amount needed, so inventory and waiting shrink — and automation with a human touch, machines that stop themselves the instant something is wrong so no person ever babysits a robot. Taiichi Ohno catalogued seven wastes: overproduction (the root of much else, since it hides every other problem), waiting, transport, over-processing, inventory, needless motion and defect rework, and he urged going to the shop floor to hunt out, one by one, every step in the value stream that adds no value. Lean turns removing waste and improving continually into a daily discipline for everyone, pulling production with kanban and letting any worker who spots a fault pull the cord and stop the line. The frame later spilled beyond the factory into software, healthcare and services, and became the parent of the lean startup's minimum-viable-product, test-fast gospel.

termEn: Theory of Constraints: Mind the Bottleneck
oneLiner: 系统的产出由最慢的那一环决定——优化非瓶颈，多半是自我安慰。
oneLinerEn: Output is set by the slowest link; optimising a non-bottleneck is largely self-soothing.
detail: 埃利亚胡·高德拉特在小说《目标》（1984）里用五步聚焦法把约束讲透：识别系统的约束（瓶颈）、让一切服从约束、挖尽约束的产能、给约束扩容、然后回到第一步，因为约束会转移。他用“有效产出、库存、运营费”三个指标取代局部效率，提醒管理者：链条的强度只看最弱一环，非瓶颈环节的“改善”若无视瓶颈，只会制造更多库存与等待。由此衍生出“鼓-缓冲-绳”的排产法：以瓶颈为鼓点调度、在瓶颈前设时间缓冲保护、用信息绳限制投入。它与精益同源而视角不同：两者都盯着流动，约束理论把瓶颈抬为改善的唯一入口。它对“处处都要改进”的直觉泼了冷水：任一时刻的瓶颈只有一个，把力气花在它身上才撬动全局。
detailEn: In the novel The Goal (1984) Eliyahu Goldratt laid out the five focusing steps: identify the system's constraint (its bottleneck), subordinate everything else to it, exploit the constraint's capacity, elevate the constraint, then return to step one, since the constraint moves. He replaced local efficiency with three measures—throughput, inventory and operating expense—warned that a chain is only as strong as its weakest link, and that "improving" a non-bottleneck while ignoring the bottleneck merely piles up inventory and waiting. From this came drum-buffer-rope scheduling: pace to the bottleneck's drum, place a time buffer ahead of it for protection, and cap releases with an information rope. It shares lean's roots but a different lens; both chase flow, while constraints theory crowns the bottleneck as the single gate to improvement.

oneLiner: 在需要的时间、按需要的量送到——用 EOQ 与看板把库存与缺货在两端之间权衡。
oneLinerEn: Deliver what is needed when it is needed — trade stock against shortages with EOQ and kanban.
detail: 库存像水库：它缓冲不确定性，却也占用资金、掩盖问题——大野耐一的比喻是“水位降下，礁石露出”。经典做法是经济订货量（EOQ），在订货成本与持有成本之间求一个平衡点；安全库存则用来应对需求与交期的波动。准时制（JIT）把这套推向极致：以“下游拉动上游”的看板信号取代提前生产，让物料按需到位。但少库存也让系统更脆——一次断供就能停线，2011 年日本地震使全球汽车与电子供应链断裂便是例证。因此 JIT 不是“库存越少越好”，而要与供应商深度协同、与风险冗余反复权衡。这也解释了为何在瘟疫与地缘冲击之后，许多企业不再一味追求零库存，而是回头补上关键料件的安全冗余。
detailEn: Inventory is a reservoir: it buffers uncertainty yet ties up capital and hides problems—Taiichi Ohno's image was that lowering the water level exposes the rocks. The classic tool is the economic order quantity (EOQ), trading ordering cost against holding cost for a balance point, while safety stock absorbs swings in demand and lead time. Just-in-time pushes this to the limit, letting a downstream-pulls-upstream kanban signal replace advance production so materials arrive as needed. But lean stock makes the system brittle—one disrupted supplier can halt a line, as the 2011 earthquake in Japan showed by snapping global auto and electronics chains. So JIT is not "less inventory is always better"; it must be paired with deep supplier coordination and a constant weighing of risk against buffer.

oneLiner: 用横条把任务排在时间轴上,一眼看清谁在何时做、进度落在哪里。
oneLinerEn: Lay tasks as bars on a timeline — who does what when, and how far along.
detail: 亨利·甘特在一战前后把这种进度图推广开来（它建立在更早的横道图与传统工程图之上），其中最被低估的发明其实是“人为成本”曲线——把已花工时与应完成工作量画在同一张图上，用于战时造船厂的问责。甘特图至今仍是项目计划的通用语言，长处在于直白：一屏就能看完“谁、在何时、做到哪”。局限也正来自直白：它只画时间不画依赖，复杂项目里“改一条、崩一片”的连锁它表达不出，于是关键路径（依赖与浮动）与里程碑、燃尽图（剩余量）需要搭着一起用。它还有两种典型病：一是把精确到日的条形当成承诺而非假设，于是每周都在改图而不是在改执行；二是过度精细的甘特会沦为“计划剧场”——图越来越好看，而无人用它做决定。判别一个甘特图是否健在很简单：图上有没有标依赖与浮动，以及上次删掉一个条形是因为它真的完成了。
detailEn: Henry Gantt popularised the chart around the First World War (building on earlier bar charts and engineering schedules), and his underrated invention was really the 'man-hour cost' curve — planned labour cost drawn against work due on the same axis, used to hold wartime shipyards accountable. The bar chart remains the common currency of project planning because it is legible: who, when, how far, in one screen. Its limits come from the same legibility. It draws time but not dependency, so in a complex project the knock-on of 'change one bar, break ten' is invisible — hence critical path (dependency and float), milestones and burndown (remaining quantity) must ride alongside. Two characteristic diseases: bars dated to the day get read as commitments rather than assumptions, so the chart is edited weekly instead of the execution; and an exhaustively detailed Gantt decays into planning theatre, prettier each sprint, used by nobody for a decision. The health test is cheap: does the file show dependencies and float at all, and when was a bar last deleted because the work actually finished?

oneLiner: 项目最短工期由最长的依赖任务链决定——这条链上的任务没有缓冲。
oneLinerEn: The shortest possible duration equals the longest dependent chain; tasks on it have no slack.
detail: 关键路径法（Kelley 与 Walker，1957 年用于杜邦检修）把任务按前后依赖连成网络，正向算最早开工、反向算最晚开工，总时差为零的那条链就是关键路径。它给管理者一个反直觉的指令：想缩短工期只能动关键路径上的任务，从富余任务往这里加人——而非“哪条看着忙帮哪条”，后者只会把非关键任务做得更漂亮而不提前完工。两个必须配套的提醒。第一，关键路径会变：一旦你压短它，下一条最长的路就接位（“共享关键路径”与多关键路径在真实项目里很常见），所以每周重算。第二，三点估计（乐观/最可能/悲观，PERT）估的是单项任务时长，而项目完工概率取决于整条路径的组合——各任务都按“最可能”排的项目，按期完工常常低于一半，这是 Brooks 定律背后的算术之一。
detailEn: The method (Kelley and Walker, for a DuPont turnaround in 1957) wires tasks into a network by precedence, computes earliest starts forwards and latest starts backwards, and calls the chain with zero total float the critical path. It hands the manager a counter-intuitive order: to finish earlier you may only act on tasks in that chain, moving resource from slack work into it — not 'help wherever looks busy', which makes non-critical work prettier and the completion date unchanged. Two riders. The critical path shifts: compress it and the next-longest chain takes over, since multiple and near-critical paths are normal in real projects, so recompute weekly. And three-point estimates (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic — PERT) describe single task durations, while the probability of finishing the project depends on the whole path: a plan built by scheduling every task at its 'most likely' duration frequently lands under fifty percent on time. That is one piece of arithmetic behind Brooks's law.

oneLiner: 把工作量可视化、限制在制品、只在有容量时才拉动——少并行、快流动。
oneLinerEn: Visualise the work, cap work in progress, pull only when there is capacity — less multitasking, faster flow.
detail: 看板源于丰田的补货卡片（大野耐一 1950 年代参照超市启发）：后道工序按需取货，取货信号向前传，过量生产因此被制度拦住。软件领域把它翻成“列—卡—限额”：用待办/进行中/已完成暴露拥堵，用在制品（WIP）上限迫使团队把手上的事做完再开新的。核心洞见来自利特尔定律的直觉：交付速度等于在制品数除以周期时间，因为在制品不降、谈提升效率都是空话；限制并行比提高各环节利用率更能提升整体流动，因为多任务并行的真正成本是切换与等待而非工作量。它也顺手提供了一套会议语言：站着把卡片从右往左讲（已完成→在做→阻塞），而不是轮流报流水账。要走形的地方也很典型：把列画成部门（开发→测试）而只限总 WIP，拥堵会藏在列间；以及取消限额的“今日特例”，特例会固化成制度。
detailEn: Kanban began as Toyota's replenishment cards (Ohno, after watching a supermarket): downstream stages withdraw what they need, the withdrawal signal travels upstream, and overproduction is blocked by mechanism rather than by exhortation. Software turned it into columns, cards and a limit: a board exposes congestion, while a work-in-progress cap forces the team to finish before starting. The core insight is Little's law felt rather than derived — throughput equals WIP divided by cycle time, so nothing improves while WIP grows, and capping concurrency moves flow further than raising each person's utilisation, because the true cost of multitasking is switching and waiting, not workload. It also ships a meeting language for free: walk the board right to left (done, doing, blocked) instead of round-robin status recital. The typical corruptions are equally clear: columns drawn as departments (dev, test) with only a total WIP cap, which hides congestion between columns, and the 'today only' exemption from the limit — exemptions have a strong tendency to become policy.

oneLiner: 让操作工也参与保养设备，追求零故障、零停机、零缺陷。
oneLinerEn: Involve operators in maintaining equipment, aiming for zero breakdowns, downtime and defects.
detail: 源自日本的全面生产维护把“维护是维修部门的事”改为全员生产维护：1951 年美国的经营性维修概念引入日本，经中岛靖一等人在日产柴油重工发展，1969 年起以“自主保养”（操作工自己做日常点检与清洁）为旗号，配计划保养、个别改善、教育培训等支柱（常归纳为八大支柱），把设备综合效率（OEE）作为核心指标，追求零故障、零废品、零事故。它与精益、六西格玛互补：精益管流动，TPM 守设备这一环的可靠，日本设备保全协会并设 TPM 奖推动。要点在于把设备交给最了解它的人，用微小停机与换型时间的消除来撑开产能。它把“意外停机”从认命变为可控，靠的是把小问题挡在酿成大故障之前。
detailEn: Originating in Japan, TPM flipped "maintenance is the repair department's job" into everyone's job: American preventive maintenance arrived in Japan in 1951, was developed by Seiichi Nakajima and others at Nippon Seiki and Nissan-Diesel, and from 1969 flew the flag of autonomous maintenance—operators doing their own daily inspection and cleaning—alongside planned maintenance, focused improvement and training under what are usually grouped as eight pillars, scoring it all with overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) in pursuit of zero breakdowns, zero defects and zero accidents. It complements lean and Six Sigma: lean manages flow, TPM secures the reliability of the equipment step, and the Japan Institute of Plant Maintenance pushes it via a TPM Award. The core move is handing machines to those who know them best and prying open capacity by erasing micro-stoppages and changeover time.

oneLiner: 把供应商到客户的整条链当作一个系统来协调——牛鞭效应是它的经典病症。
oneLinerEn: Manage the supplier-to-customer chain as one system — the bullwhip effect is its classic ailment.
detail: 供应链管理跨企业协调采购、生产、仓储、物流与信息流，目标说得像口令：以对的量、在对的时间到对的地方。它最著名的发现是牛鞭效应（Forrester 1961，其名为“需求放大”）：需求信号沿链上溯被逐级放大，因过度预测、批量订货、价格浮动恐慌囤货与短缺下的双重订购而失真——宝洁尿布研究中“零售小幅波动、厂方大幅波动”一例已成经典。解法都是往“透明”与“短”上用力：共享实时销售数据、缩短提前期（比压库存更根本）、供应商管理库存（VMI）、延迟策略（把差异化推到尽可能后置）。但要补一条二十年代的现实：效率与韧性的目标函数变了。长期只优化周转与成本会把链条拉得很紧，于是一次断供就全线停摆；今天主流口径是“效率为基、韧性为顶”——多源、近岸与关键件安全库存不是浪费，而是为一小概率事件买的保险，保费要真的算过再买。
detailEn: Supply chain management coordinates purchasing, production, warehousing, logistics and information across firm boundaries, stated like a slogan: the right quantity, at the right time, in the right place. Its signature finding is the bullwhip (Forrester 1961, under the name demand amplification): a demand signal is magnified stage by stage as it travels upstream, through over-forecasting, batch ordering, price-driven panic stocking and double ordering during shortages — the Pampers-diaper case, small swing at retail and a large one at the factory, has become the canonical illustration. The remedies all push toward transparency and shortness: share point-of-sale data, cut lead time (more fundamental than squeezing inventory), vendor-managed inventory, and postponement, deferring differentiation as late as possible. Add the reality that arrived in the 2020s: the objective function changed. Optimising turnover and cost alone stretches the chain so taut that one break stops everything, hence the current framing of efficiency as base and resilience as ceiling — multi-sourcing, nearshoring and safety stock for critical parts are not waste but insurance against a low-probability event, and the premium should actually be computed before it is bought.

oneLiner: 整理、整顿、清扫、清洁、素养——先管好工位，再谈改善文化。
oneLinerEn: Sort, set in order, shine, standardise, sustain — tidy the workplace before chasing a culture of improvement.
detail: 5S 源自丰田（整理、整顿、清扫、清洁、素养，日文各以“S”开头），是精益最基础的入门纪律：清除不要之物（整理）、每样东西有固定位置且一目了然（整顿）、保持干净并借清扫暴露异常（清扫）、把前三者制度化、定成标准（清洁）、靠习惯与自律长期维持（素养）。看似“大扫除”，实则是让问题一眼可见、减少寻找与搬运浪费的地基，也是检验团队能否坚持小纪律的试金石。医院推行 5S 后能降低给药差错与院感，办公室套用则减少找文档、找工具的时间。它的精髓不在一次彻底打扫，而在把“看得见异常”的秩序长期固化下来。少了最后的素养一环，前四步往往在检查过后迅速回潮，5S 因此最考验的其实是管理层的长期坚持。
detailEn: 5S comes from Toyota (seiri, seiton, seiso, seiketsu, shitsuke—five Japanese words each starting with "S") as lean's most basic entry discipline: clear out what is unneeded (sort), give every item a fixed, obvious place (set in order), keep things clean and use cleaning to surface anomalies (shine), institutionalize the first three into standards (standardize), and sustain it by habit and self-discipline (sustain). It looks like spring-cleaning but is really the ground work that makes problems visible at a glance and cuts the waste of searching and carrying—and a touchstone for whether a team can hold small disciplines. Hospitals adopting 5S cut medication errors and infections; offices apply it to reclaim time lost hunting for files and tools. Its point is not one deep clean but freezing an order that reveals anomalies and keeping it for the long haul.

oneLiner: 用物理或流程设计让错误根本犯不出来，而不是靠人加倍小心。
oneLinerEn: Design the product or process so mistakes cannot be made, rather than asking people to be more careful.
detail: 新乡重夫提出的防错法（早期他称之为“无缺陷控制系统”）：通过接触式、定数量式、动作步序式等装置，让零件装反就装不进、少一步就开不了机、漏装则流水线自动停机。它把质量从“事后检验、依赖注意力”转为“源头杜绝”，成本极低却极有效——从只能一个方向插入的旧式接口、微波炉开门即断电，到工厂里形状唯一的治具都是它。与 5Why 呼应：与其事后追责粗心的人，不如改设计让粗心也无从犯错。它的高明处在于把“人总会犯错”这个前提摊开，用机制而非意志力去兜住。相比昂贵而繁琐的自动检测，这类物理防呆往往几乎零成本，却在源头就掐断了错误流向下游的路径，也是“质量无需检验”最朴素的落地。
detailEn: Shigeo Shingo's poka-yoke (which he first called a zero-quality-control system) uses contact, fixed-count and motion-step devices so that a part reversed simply will not fit, a skipped step keeps the machine from starting, and a missed component halts the line. It converts quality from after-the-fact inspection that leans on attention into source-level prevention—cheap yet potent, from keyed connectors that fit only one way, to a microwave that cuts power when opened, to form-specific jigs on the line. It echoes the 5 Whys: rather than blame a careless person afterward, change the design so carelessness has nowhere to bite. Its insight is to accept that people will err and to catch that with mechanism, not willpower.

oneLiner: 小步快跑、频繁交付、边做边学：用短周期迭代和跨职能小队替代层层审批的大计划。
oneLinerEn: Ship in short iterations with a cross-functional squad — deliver often, learn fast — instead of one heavily approved master plan.
detail: 《敏捷宣言》(2001)重估价值观：个体互动高于流程工具、可工作的产品高于庞杂文档、客户协作高于合同谈判、响应变化高于死守计划。Scrum 是其框架之一：产品负责人排定待办、开发团队在固定冲刺(常 2 周)内交付增量，辅以每日站会、评审与回顾持续改进；角色精简、强调自组织与可视化。它特别适合需求不定、要快速试错的领域，但并非万能——安全关键、强监管或需求稳定的项目用传统瀑布更合适；看板(同为拉动、限流)与它同源互补。
detailEn: The Agile Manifesto (2001) re-ranked values — individuals and interactions over process, working product over heavy docs, customer collaboration over contracting, responding to change over following a plan. Scrum is one framework within it: a Product Owner ranks the backlog, a team delivers an increment in fixed Sprints (often two weeks), and daily stand-ups, reviews and retrospectives drive continual improvement — few roles, self-organising and visual. It suits domains of shifting, fast-try requirements but is not universal; safety-critical, heavily regulated or stable-need work can favour waterfall. Kanban (both pull, both limit work in progress) is kin and complementary.

oneLiner: 画清一个产品从下单到交付的全流程，把增值时间与非增值的等待、返工、库存逐一揪出来。
oneLinerEn: Map the whole flow from order to delivery to expose value-adding time versus the waiting, rework and inventory that add none.
detail: 价值流图源自丰田生产方式，由卢福与舒克在《学习观察》一书中整理普及：它要求沿着物料与信息两条流，把每道工序一一画下，标注加工周期、批量、换型时间、在制品与等待，从而得到两个对照鲜明的数字——从下单到交付的“总交付周期”，以及只占其中极小一段（常常不足百分之一）的“增值时间”。这张图的力量，在于把“浪费”从一句口号变成触目可见的比例，团队据此设计理想中的“未来状态图”、并排出通往它的改善路线图与优先次序。它被称为精益的“诊断 X 光片”，常与看板（按需拉动）、约束理论（先找瓶颈）、价值链（从整条链看利润）配套使用，避免只优化了局部某道工序、却拖慢了整体的流动。
detailEn: Value-stream mapping comes from the Toyota system and was codified and spread by Rother and Shook in Learning to See: tracing both the material and the information flow, it draws every step in turn, noting cycle time, batch, changeover, work-in-process and waiting, to yield two starkly contrasting figures — the total lead time from order to delivery, and the value-added time that is typically only a sliver of it (often under a percent). The map's power is turning waste from a slogan into a ratio you can see, so the team designs an ideal future-state map and lays out an improvement path and priority toward it. It is called lean's diagnostic X-ray, used alongside kanban (pull on demand), the theory of constraints (find the bottleneck first) and the value chain (read profit across the whole arc), so as not to optimise one local step while slowing the flow of the whole.

oneLiner: 让状态一眼可见：看板、标线、颜色与图表，把“是否正常”摆在墙上而非藏在报表里。
oneLinerEn: Make the status visible at a glance — boards, lines, colours and charts that put 'normal or not' on the wall, not buried in a report.
detail: 目视化管理把信息做成即时、直观、人人可读的视觉信号：地面标线划定该放什么、通道走哪里，安灯拉绳让任何一线工人发现问题都能一键停线，看板卡显式标出在制数量与节拍，状态灯与红线让“本该做的改善”自己跳出来。它的目标不是贴满图表好看，而是让异常无需解释也能被一眼识别、并立刻触发动作——把“要不要报告、谁来判断”的延迟压到最低。好的看板遵循一条原则：信息要放在使用它的人眼前，而不是锁进办公室。它与 5S（先理出秩序）、防错（在源头杜绝）、看板拉动同属精益家族，共同撑起“让问题无处藏身”的地基：先让问题暴露出来，改进才有的放矢。
detailEn: Visual management turns information into immediate, at-a-glance signals anyone can read: floor lines mark where things belong and walkways run, an Andon cord lets any worker on the line stop production the moment they spot a problem, Kanban cards show work-in-progress and takt, and status lights and red-lines make the improvement that is due jump out on its own. The aim is not charts for their own sake but anomalies that need no explaining and prompt action at once — driving to near zero the delay of "should I report this, and who will judge". A good board follows one rule: put information in front of the person who uses it, not locked in an office. With 5S (order first), Poka-Yoke (prevent at source) and Kanban (pull) it belongs to the lean family, together laying the foundation for leaving problems nowhere to hide — only once a problem is exposed can it be fixed with intent.

oneLiner: 少数关键、多数次要：约八成结果来自两成原因——先攻那决定性的少数。
oneLinerEn: The vital few, the trivial many — roughly 80 percent of effect comes from 20 percent of causes, so attack the decisive minority first.
detail: 意大利经济学家帕累托观察到本国约八成财富握于两成人手中，约瑟夫·朱兰把这种普遍的不平衡提炼为“八零／二零法则”（或“关键少数、次要多数”）并引入质量管理：多数缺陷来自少数成因、多数销售来自少数客户、多数故障来自少数环节、多数投诉来自少数问题。它并非精确的数字配比，而是一种“投入与产出天然不均、不平衡才是常态”的心智，提醒别把力气平均撒在所有事上。配上帕累托图——按频次降序排列的柱状叠加累计百分比曲线——就能一眼“把关键的少数挑出来”，让有限的资源投向最能起效的地方。它是优先级排序、ABC 库存分类、根因分析、以及各类“要事第一、抓重点”背后的通用逻辑，但也须警惕因过度聚焦头部而忽视长尾与系统性成因。
detailEn: The Italian economist Pareto observed that about eighty percent of his country's wealth sat with twenty percent of its people; Joseph Juran distilled this pervasive imbalance into the eighty-twenty rule (the vital few and the trivial many) and brought it into quality management: most defects stem from few causes, most sales from few customers, most failures from few steps, most complaints from few problems. It is not a precise ratio but a mindset that input and output are inherently uneven and imbalance is the norm, a warning not to spread effort evenly over everything. With a Pareto chart — bars ranked high-to-low overlaid by a cumulative-percentage curve — you can separate the vital few at a glance and point scarce resources at what truly moves. It is the shared logic behind prioritisation, ABC inventory classification, root-cause work and every put-first-things-first advice, though one must guard against ignoring the long tail and systemic causes by over-focusing on the head.

oneLiner: 范围、时间、成本(和质量)互相牵制:动一头,必得松另一头。
oneLinerEn: Scope, time and cost (and quality) constrain each other: move one and you must ease another.
detail: 项目三角也称“约束三角”：任何项目都由范围（做什么）、时间（多久交付）、成本（花多少、投几人）三条边夹定，质量坐落在正中央。它道出一个残酷却诚实的取舍——“多、快、好、省”不可同时全得：要提前上线，就得砍范围或加人加钱；要压成本，就得多花时间或缩范围；要扩范围，时间与成本必有一头让步。它的价值不在公式本身，而在给谈判与期望管理提供了一套共同语言：当客户一边要求“加需求”、一边坚持“不改期也不加价”时，用三角把代价摆到台面上，避免把矛盾留给交付那天爆发。甘特图、关键路径与敏捷的迭代取舍，背后都是同一组约束——真正成熟的项目管理，是主动选择牺牲哪一条边，而不是幻想三条边同时不动。
detailEn: The project triangle, also the triple constraint, fences every project with three edges — scope (what gets built), time (how long to deliver) and cost (how much money and how many people) — with quality sitting at the centre. It states a blunt but honest trade-off: you cannot have more, faster, better and cheaper all at once; to launch sooner you cut scope or add people and money, to squeeze cost you spend more time or reduce scope, and to grow scope you concede on time or cost. Its worth is not the diagram but the shared language it gives negotiation and expectation management: when a client demands more features while refusing to move the date or the price, the triangle puts the real cost on the table instead of saving the row for delivery day. Gantt, critical path and agile iteration all rest on this same set of constraints — mature project management is choosing which edge to bend on purpose, not pretending all three can stay fixed at once.

oneLiner: 把大项目逐层切成可交付的小块,直到每块都能估、能派、能验——先拆再做。
oneLinerEn: Slice a big project level by level into deliverables you can estimate, assign and verify — decompose before you build.
detail: 工作分解结构（WBS）靠一条“百分之百规则”把项目自上而下拆成越来越细的工作包：每个下级合起来要完整覆盖其上级、既不重叠也不遗漏，拆到每一块都小到能估算成本与工期、能指定唯一负责人、能明确验收。它是整个项目管理的骨架——进度（甘特图）、预算、责任分工（RACI）和风险登记，最终都挂在同一棵分解树上；先有了分解，后面的计划才谈得上可信。它专门对抗那种“一上来就想统筹全流程”的失控：再复杂的项目，只有在结构被拆清楚之后才变得可管理。常见的坑是分解过度沦为微观管理、或漏掉收尾、培训、集成这类不直接产出交付物却必需的支路，故每一层都要验收“加总是否仍等于上层的百分之百”。
detailEn: The Work Breakdown Structure decomposes a project top-down into ever-finer work packages under a single hundred percent rule: the children of any node must together fully cover their parent, nothing duplicated and nothing missing, until each package is small enough to cost, to schedule, to own with one name and to accept. It is the skeleton of all project management — the schedule (Gantt), the budget, the RACI responsibility split and the risk register all hang from this same decomposition tree, and only once the break-down exists can a plan be trusted. It counters the urge to hold the whole flow in your head at once: however complex, a project becomes manageable only after its structure is laid out. The usual traps are decomposing so far it turns into micromanagement, or omitting branches that ship no visible deliverable yet are essential, such as closeout, training and integration, so check at every level that the parts still sum to the whole hundred percent.

oneLiner: 把最佳做法写成人人可照做的固定步骤,让质量不依赖“某个老师傅记得”。
oneLinerEn: Write the best known method into fixed steps anyone can follow, so quality stops depending on some veteran remembering.
detail: 标准作业程序（SOP）把一项工作“当前公认最好的做法”固化成可复现的步骤、标准与检查点。它的好处是可培训、可交接、可审计、能压缩因人而异的变异，是把个人经验变成组织资产的最低门槛手段（与野中提出的知识“外化”、与知识工作者一脉相连），也是精益“先标准化、才谈得上持续改善”的前提——没有基准线，改进就无从衡量。真正的风险不是没人照做，而是不小心把一套早已过时的做法锁死成了标准：所以 SOP 必须定期回看、明确版本与负责人，并留一条“偏离上报”的通道——一线发现更优做法时能反馈，而不是默默各自变通，让“标准”与“实际”越走越远。
detailEn: A Standard Operating Procedure freezes a task's current best-known way of working into repeatable steps, standards and checkpoints. Its payoff is trainability, handover, auditability and less person-to-person variation — the lowest-barrier way to turn individual know-how into an organisational asset (kin to Nonaka's externalisation of knowledge and to the knowledge worker), and the precondition of lean's standardise-first-then-improve, since without a baseline improvement cannot be measured. The real risk is not that no one follows it but that a long-outdated method gets locked in as the standard, so an SOP must be reviewed on a cadence, carry a clear version and owner, and keep a channel to flag deviations — so that when the floor finds a better way it feeds back, rather than each person quietly working around it and letting the standard and what actually happens drift ever further apart.

oneLiner: 面对复杂又易错的事,靠一张简短清单兜底,而不是靠专家的“脑子记住”。
oneLinerEn: For complex, error-prone work, let a short checklist catch what experts' memory cannot, rather than trusting recall.
detail: 外科医生阿图·葛文德发现：现代工作的失败常非因无知，而在“知道却漏做”——复杂性、不确定性与时间压力压垮了人的记忆与疏忽防线。他借航空业“起飞前检查清单”的成功，为世界卫生组织设计了手术安全清单（切皮前核对身份、部位、过敏、备血、团队沟通），在多国八家医院试点，术后死亡率与并发症显著下降。要点很克制：清单只列“关键、易漏”的少数几项，分清“检查—确认”（做完再打勾）与“朗读—执行”（边读边做）两类流程，绝不写成百科；更要配套“照单办事、也敢于叫停”的文化，否则清单沦为走过场。它是把已知变成“必然被做”的低成本、高杠杆工具，也适用于系统上线、交接、急诊与软件开发。
detailEn: Surgeon Atul Gawande found that modern failure is often not ignorance but knowing and still missing it — complexity, uncertainty and time pressure overwhelm memory and our defences against slips. Borrowing aviation's pre-flight checklist he designed, for the World Health Organization, a surgical safety checklist (confirming identity, site, allergies, blood and team communication before the cut), piloted in eight hospitals across countries, where deaths and complications fell markedly. The craft is deliberately spare: list only the few critical, easily-skipped items, distinguish do-confirmation (tick after doing) from read-do (act as you read), and never write an encyclopaedia; above all pair it with a culture of following the list yet daring to halt, or it degrades into ritual. It is a low-cost, high-leverage way to turn what is known into what reliably gets done, and it fits go-lives, handoffs, emergencies and software too.

oneLiner: 凡是可能出错,终究会出错——别指望侥幸,要为失败设计。
oneLinerEn: Whatever can go wrong will go wrong — do not count on luck; design for failure.
detail: 墨菲定律那句“凡是可能出错的，终究会出错”，源自 1949 年爱德华·墨菲参与的一项火箭减速工程测试——因传感器全部接反而得出的牢骚，后来却成了风险文化的箴言。它的工程含义绝非宿命论，而是一种统计式的提醒：只要一个环节存在出错的可能，在足够多次尝试、足够复杂的系统里，小概率失误迟早会显现，所以绝不该把“总不至于吧”当作设计依据。真正成熟的应对，是把墨菲当成设计输入而非事后借口——关键处做冗余备份、上线前防错设计、正式决策前先做“事前验尸”预想失败、发布走灰度放量、把最坏情况纳入测试。它教人谦卑地预先为出错留好退路，而不是事后懊恼，与防错、反脆弱、事前验尸这些思路本是一脉相承。
detailEn: Murphy's law — whatever can go wrong will go wrong — traces to a 1949 rocket-sled engineering test Edward Murphy was involved in, born of the gripe that every sensor had been wired backwards, yet it became a maxim of risk culture. Its engineering meaning is not fatalism but a statistical warning: wherever a chance of error exists, across enough trials and enough complexity the low-probability slip will eventually surface, so you must never lean on "surely that won't happen" as a design assumption. The mature response is to feed Murphy in as design input rather than excuse it after the fact — build redundancy into critical points, mistake-proof before launch, run a pre-mortem to picture the failure before committing, roll out in stages, and test the worst case on purpose. It teaches people to humbly leave a way out of error in advance instead of rueing it later, kin in spirit to mistake-proofing, antifragility and the pre-mortem.

oneLiner: 别等出事才补救：逐项预判产品或流程可能怎样失效、后果多严重、多难发现，按风险优先改进。
oneLinerEn: Do not fix only after failure: predict how each part of a product or process can fail, how severe and how hard to catch, then fix by risk priority.
detail: 失效模式与影响分析起源于军用标准与航天工程、后被制造业与医疗广泛采用，是一种“事前”而非“事后”的前瞻性风险工具。做法是把系统逐级拆解到部件与工序，逐一列出每个环节可能的失效模式、后果与成因，再对每一项分别按严重度、发生概率、可探测性三项打分（常取一到十分）并相乘得“风险优先数”，据以优先处置高分项，并把分析固化成随设计变更而持续更新的活文档。它把“哪里可能出错”从模糊直觉变成一张可排序、可追责的行动清单，常与防错（造之前就让它错不成）、事前验尸（在想象中先让项目失败再倒推）互补。局限在于打分难免主观、易沦为填表作业，必须靠跨职能团队与真实故障数据来支撑，否则只会自我安慰。
detailEn: Failure mode and effects analysis, born in military and space standards and since taken up across manufacturing and healthcare, is a forward-looking risk tool that looks before things break rather than after. Break the system down level by level into parts and steps, list for each the ways it might fail, its effects and its causes, then score each on severity, occurrence and detectability (often one to ten) and multiply them into a risk priority number, act on the highest first, and keep the analysis as a living document updated whenever the design changes. It turns where this might go wrong from vague intuition into a rankable, assignable action list, complementing mistake-proofing (make it physically impossible to err before building) and the pre-mortem (imagine the project has already failed and reason backwards). Its limits: scoring is subjective and it can decay into box-ticking, so it needs a cross-functional team and real failure data behind it, or it becomes self-consolation.

oneLiner: 为什么高峰期总在等？用数学刻画到达与服务能力的失衡，在多开窗口与少让人等之间找平衡。
oneLinerEn: Why does waiting spike at rush hour? Model the mismatch between arrivals and service capacity, and balance adding servers against sparing the queue.
detail: 源于丹麦电话工程师爱尔朗早年对通话等待与交换机负载的研究，后成运筹学与排队论分支。它用到达间隔、服务时间分布、窗口（服务台）数量与服务规则（先入先出、优先、抢占）为排队建模，量化平均等待、队列长度、系统利用率与流失概率；核心结论是非线性的：当负荷逼近饱和、利用率趋近满位，等待时间不是线性而是急剧飙升——这正是餐厅、呼叫中心、医院急诊、服务器与路网“越忙越慢”的根源。根本权衡在于提升利用率与缩短等待互相拉扯：加资源能减排队却增成本、且抬高空闲。它提醒运营者别把系统常年逼近满负荷，要为随机波动留出余量，并以分流、并行、预约与预期管理改善体验。
detailEn: Born from the Danish telephone engineer Erlang's early study of call waiting and exchange load, later a branch of operations research. It models queues from inter-arrival time, service-time distribution, the number of servers and the discipline (first-in-first-out, priority, preemption), quantifying average wait, queue length, utilisation and loss; the central result is non-linear — as load nears saturation and utilisation approaches full, waiting does not rise gently but blows up, the very reason restaurants, call centres, emergency rooms, servers and road networks crawl when busy. The core tension is that higher utilisation and shorter waits pull against each other: more capacity cuts the queue but raises cost and idle time. It warns operators never to pin a system at full load year-round but to keep slack for random variance, and to improve experience through routing, parallelism, appointments and expectation management.

oneLiner: 在坏品造出来之前就叫停：用控制图区分过程的偶然波动与异常信号，让质量靠数据而非事后检验。
oneLinerEn: Stop before defects are made: use control charts to tell routine variation from special-cause signals, so quality rides on data, not after-the-fact inspection.
detail: 休哈特把统计过程控制（SPC）做成质量的地基：任何过程都自带正常波动（共同原因），但一旦点子越出上下控制限，或出现连续上升、连续偏离中心这类模式，就说明混入了可追查的特殊原因。控制图的价值，正是把这两类信号干净分开，让一线在问题成灾前就识别并纠正，而不是靠事后全数检验把废品剔除出去。它是六西格玛与统计质量管理的重要组成，也划出一条常被忽略的界线——“稳定”不等于“合格”：一个过程完全可以稳定地、可预测地生产废品。所以顺序不能反：先让过程受控、消除特殊原因，再谈改进均值、收窄波动与做能力分析，否则只是在噪声里瞎调，越调越偏。
detailEn: Shewhart made statistical process control the foundation of quality: every process carries its own common-cause variation, but once a point falls outside the upper and lower control limits, or shows runs, trends or shifts off centre, a special, assignable cause has entered. The value of the control chart is precisely to split these two signals cleanly, so the floor corrects a problem before defects pile up rather than sorting them out afterwards by blanket inspection. It underpins six sigma and statistical quality control and draws a line often missed — being in control is not the same as being up to spec: a process can be perfectly stable, predictably making scrap. So the order cannot be reversed: first bring the process under control and remove special causes, only then tune the mean, narrow the variation and assess capability, or you are just fiddling in noise.

oneLiner: 把设备换型时间压到个位数分钟：分清内外部作业、把内部动作尽量外移并标准化，小批量才划算。
oneLinerEn: Shrink changeover to single-digit minutes: split internal from external work, move internal steps out and standardise them, so small batches pay off.
detail: 快速换模（SMED）由新乡重夫在丰田一线、经大野耐一的推动总结而成，是精益应对“多品种、小批量”的关键一环。核心手法是先把一次换模的所有步骤严格拆成两类：必须在停机时才能做的“内部作业”，与可以在机器还在运转时提前备好的“外部作业”；再尽可能把内部作业搬到外部去做、让多项准备并行推进、以标准化容器与预定位夹具取消反复调试、把每一步剩余时间逐一压缩。换型越快，经济批量就能越小、在制品库存越低、对多样需求的响应越快，而不必靠大批量来摊薄切换成本。它把“换线很慢”从一条看似不可逾越的技术极限，变成可以无止境改善的流程，也直接支撑了准时化生产与看板拉动。
detailEn: The single-minute exchange of die was worked out by Shigeo Shingo on the Toyota floor under Taiichi Ohno's drive, and is a keystone of how lean copes with many products in small lots. The core move is to split every step of a changeover strictly into two kinds: internal work that can only be done with the machine stopped, and external work that can be prepared in advance while it still runs; then shift as much internal work to external as possible, run the preparations in parallel, kill repeated adjustment with standardised caddies and pre-set locating fixtures, and shave each remaining step one by one. The faster the changeover, the smaller the economic batch can be, the lower the work-in-process and the quicker the answer to varied demand, without leaning on big lots to amortise setup. It turns changeover-is-slow from a hard technical limit into a process that can be improved endlessly, and it directly underpins just-in-time production and kanban pull.
